sections.h2: Which county holds your Tualatin parcel?
sections.html:
Tualatin is a southwestern suburb of Portland, just south of Tigard, with the Tualatin River along most of its northern edge. Most of the city is in Washington County, and a small piece is in Clackamas County. The ZIP code is 97062.

That split is the first thing to settle. It decides who sends the tax bill and which recorder handles the deed. Look at your tax statement to see which county bills the parcel.

The population estimate for July 1, 2025 is 28,139, up from 27,942 in 2020.

With 45% of homes rented in the 2020 count, many Tualatin sellers are landlords. A rental with a tenant in place, deferred repairs or a long vacancy can be harder to list than a move-in-ready owner-occupied house.

The city plan defines the floodplain as the area covered by the 1% annual chance (100-year) flood on FEMA maps. The northern edge follows the river, so parcels there are the ones to check. A buyer or lender may ask whether the house sits inside it.

  • Protected natural areas. The Hedges Creek Wetland and the Tonquin Scablands are named protected environmental areas.
  • Basalt Creek. A planning area to the south, with a concept plan adopted April 22, 2019 and a parks plan adopted August 12, 2024.
  • Housing density. Policy 3.1.1 sets at least 8 dwelling units per net acre citywide and supports duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, cottages and accessory dwelling units.

The density policy is why an owner of a larger lot sometimes has more options than a simple sale. A planner can say whether your zone permits an added unit.

A few older buildings remain downtown, among them the Sweek House (1858), the Wesch House and Little White House (1890), the Robinson Store (1912) and Tualatin Methodist Church (1926). If your house is near the old center, ask the city whether any historic review applies.

Industrial land is a major local and regional employment center. The Southwest Tualatin manufacturing district and the Medical Center district both carry large-parcel minimums, and Legacy Meridian Park Hospital is in the city. A house close to these districts can see truck traffic and shift-change commuting, which buyers notice during showings.

Most Tualatin parcels get a Washington County bill, while the small slice inside Clackamas County gets one from that county. Both use three due dates in November, February and May, with a 3% discount for paying in full and 2% for two-thirds.

Taxes follow assessed value, which is the lower of real market value or maximum assessed value, and maximum assessed value usually rises no more than 3% a year. Compression limits operating taxes to $5.00 per $1,000 of real market value for schools and $10.00 per $1,000 for local government.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Tualatin sale
sections.html:
Washington County puts a $1 per $1,000 tax on the selling price of Tualatin property. The money, or an exemption claim, is due within 15 days after recording. Gifts, inheritances, foreclosure deeds and court-ordered transfers are exempt.

ORS 306.815 generally bars cities and counties from taxing the transfer of real property, with exceptions that include a tax in effect on March 31, 1997. If your parcel is in the Clackamas County sliver, ask the title company which rules cover that address.

The Tigard-Tualatin School District covers most of Tualatin, including Bridgeport, Byrom and Tualatin elementary schools, Hazelbrook Middle School and Tualatin High School. A small section lies in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District, where students usually attend Stafford Primary.

Interstates 5 and 205, Highway 99W and Highway 217 all serve the city. WES commuter rail stops at Tualatin Station, and TriMet runs bus lines 36, 37, 38, 76, 96 and 97. Tualatin Valley Fire and Rescue provides fire and medical service.

sections.h2: Selling a Tualatin house for cash
sections.html:
Selling for cash means the buyer purchases the house in its present state and a title company closes it. The path runs from a property review to an offer, a signed contract, title work and a recorded deed.

The state's disclosure rules stay in force unless an exclusion fits, and a buyer holds five business days after getting the form to revoke. Request the closing statement ahead of time to see the proration and transfer tax lines.

Collect the lease, the end date and the deposit record. Tell the tenant in writing when you plan to sell, and decide whether the buyer takes the tenant or the house is empty at closing. A short vacancy to make repairs may help the sale, while a long one costs you taxes and utilities.

• Photo ID matching the deed.
  • The most recent tax statement, from the correct county.
  • Lender and loan number for any payoff.
  • Papers for permits and past repairs.
  • FEMA or floodplain information if the house is near the river.

sections.h2: Where a Tualatin sale tends to get stuck
sections.html: Three things slow most sales in town. The first is the county question: a seller who sends the tax bill or deed to the wrong office loses days. The second is flood or habitat paperwork on parcels near the river or a creek, where a buyer may want maps before agreeing to terms. The third is the tenant, when a rental house has a lease that ends after the date the buyer wants. Settling each of these before you accept an offer keeps escrow on schedule.

sections.h2: Property tax you may still owe
sections.html: Overdue tax is paid from your proceeds at closing, with interest, so ask the title company for a payoff figure early. Interest on late payments runs 1.333% per month under state rules. Knowing the exact figure before you accept an offer shows what you will take home.

A title or escrow company arranges the signing. The buyer's funds arrive, the deed is recorded, and your mortgage payoff, unpaid taxes, the tax proration and any county transfer tax are settled from the price. You receive the rest. In a cash sale, no lender sets the date, so it can follow your moving plans.

faqs.q: Is Tualatin in Washington County or Clackamas County?
faqs.a: Mostly Washington County, with a small portion in Clackamas County. Check your tax statement or the county assessor's record to see which one bills your parcel.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Tualatin?
faqs.a: $628,200 for owner-occupied homes, based on 2020 to 2024 estimates. That is a citywide figure, not a value for a specific house.

faqs.q: Which school district is Tualatin in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Tigard-Tualatin School District. A small section is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District.

faqs.q: Does Tualatin have a transfer tax?
faqs.a: For property in Washington County, the county charges $1 per $1,000 of the selling price. Buyer and seller decide who pays it in their contract.

faqs.q: Do I need FEMA flood information to sell a Tualatin house near the river?
faqs.a: It helps. The city plan uses FEMA maps to define the 100-year floodplain, and a buyer or lender may ask whether the house sits inside it.
